info.name: Unny API
info.description:
Final year project archive & collaboration platform.

Run folders top-to-bottom against the Unny Local environment: 01 Auth creates a student, a second collaborator student, and a supervisor and stores their tokens automatically. Later folders chain off the ids/tokens those requests save into the environment (projectId, tagId, collaborationId, supervisionRequestId, uploadKey, notificationId), so running requests out of order will fail until their dependencies have run once.

Typical happy-path demo order:
1. Auth: register student, collaborator, supervisor
2. Tags: create a tag
3. Projects: create draft project
4. Uploads: presign project file (simulates attaching the report)
5. Supervision: request supervision -> supervisor accepts
6. Projects: submit project for review
7. Reviews: supervisor approves
8. Projects: explore -> the project now appears in the public archive

v1.1 — added '10 Local Storage Fallback' folder covering the S3/local-disk auto-fallback upload path.

Run this only after: (1) a supervisor has ACCEPTED a supervision request for this project, and (2) a report file has been attached via the Uploads folder.
Only works while the project is still DRAFT — disabled once submitted.
Returns a presigned S3 PUT URL. Upload the PDF with a separate PUT request directly to `uploadUrl` (outside this API) before calling Submit Project For Review.
Called by the invited student, not the project owner.
Accepting sets this supervisor as the project's assigned supervisor, unlocking submission.
Requires the project to be PENDING_REVIEW (i.e. already submitted). On approval, a .docx certificate is generated and the project becomes publicly discoverable via Explore.
Alternative to Approve — run one or the other, not both, against the same PENDING_REVIEW project.

item.name: 10 Local Storage Fallback
Presign Project File Upload (S3 or Local — auto)

request.description: Same endpoint as the one in the '05 Uploads' folder — duplicated here so this folder can be run standalone. The backend decides S3 vs. local automatically based on whether AWS_S3_BUCKET/credentials are set (src/services/storage.service.js). This request detects which one you got back and stores it in {{storageBackend}}.

exec: console.log('Storage backend in use:', isLocal ? 'local disk (S3 not configured)' : 'S3');

item.name: Upload File To Storage (S3 or Local)

request.description:
PUTs the raw file body directly to the presigned/signed URL captured by the previous request — no Bearer token needed, exactly like an S3 presigned PUT (the URL itself is the credential). Works unchanged whether {{uploadUrl}} points at S3 or at this server's own /local-storage route.

MANUAL STEP: in the Body tab, click 'Select File' and choose a real PDF before sending — Postman cannot attach a file to a raw PUT body from a collection JSON file automatically.

If {{storageBackend}} is 'local', the file is written under LOCAL_STORAGE_DIR on the server (default storage/uploads) with a signature + expiry check enforced by src/routes/local-storage.routes.js.
Reuses the standard project-detail endpoint to confirm fileKey/fileUrl were recorded regardless of which storage backend handled the upload.
